race_context: The office on the ballot, 'Ohio County Community School Board', is the board of the Rising Sun-Ohio County Community School Corporation, which runs Rising Sun High School, Rising Sun Middle School and Ohio County Elementary School in Rising Sun; Rising Sun High School is the only high school in Ohio County {in_list}{rso_home}{wiki_rshs}. State enrollment counts were 854 students in 2023-24, 831 in 2024-25 and 801 in 2025-26 {idoe_enroll}.

The board has five members: Corey Potts, Renee Cole, Connie Smith, Gary Kinnett and Andrea Kirkpatrick {rso_board}{rso_min_20260113}. In January 2026 the board kept its 2025 officers: Potts as president, Cole as vice president and Smith as secretary {rso_min_20260113}. (The district's board page lists Kinnett, not Cole, as vice president {rso_board}.) Regular meetings are held on the second Tuesday of each month {rso_min_20260113}.

How seats are elected: Ohio County's official 2022 general-election results list 'Ohio County Community School Board Member District 4 - Vote for Two (2) Only'; Connie L. Smith was the only candidate and received 1,240 votes {oc_2022}. Gary Kinnett was already serving on the board in November 2022 and has served since {rso_min_20221108}{rso_min_20230110}. This guide did not find the district's board organization plan or a 2026 sample ballot, so the number of District 4 seats on the 2026 ballot is not confirmed.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the state list shows one District 4 race, 'vote for 1', with two candidates, Connie Lou (Williams) Smith and Gary E Kinnett, both Nonpartisan {in_list}. Both are current board members {rso_board}{rso_min_20260113}. If District 4 again elects two members, as in 2022, both incumbents could be returned; if only one seat is on the ballot, the race pits two sitting members against each other {oc_2022}{in_list}.

Budget: after a public hearing with no public comments on Sept. 23, 2025, the board approved the 2026 budget, a 2026 capital projects plan and a 2026 bus replacement plan on Oct. 14, 2025 {rso_min_20250923}{rso_min_20251014}. In June 2026 it set a Sept. 15, 2026 public hearing and Sept. 29, 2026 adoption date for the 2027 budget {rso_min_20260609}. This guide found no reporting on how the 2025 property-tax law SEA 1 affects the corporation, and no referendum.

Building projects and borrowing: on Aug. 19, 2025 the board held a public hearing on general obligation (GO) bonds, heard no comments, and approved the bonds; the superintendent updated the board on a construction project and the gym floor at the same meeting {rso_min_20250819}. In April 2026 he described upcoming projects including a high school cafeteria HVAC project and replacing cafeteria refrigerators and freezers {rso_min_20260414}.

Staff pay: the 2025-26 teacher agreement, heard on Oct. 28, 2025 and approved Nov. 4, 2025, included a $700 raise, a $500 stipend and a $300 raise for teachers with the Early Literacy Endorsement {rso_min_20251028}{rso_min_20251104}. The board also approved a 1% raise and $250 stipend for qualifying classified staff, with all stipends paid from the Rainy Day Fund, and agreed to cover half (2.5%) of a 5% health insurance premium increase {rso_min_20251104}.

Administration: in April 2026 the board approved an administrative restructuring (a new high school principal, an assistant principal who is also corporation athletic director, and a dean of students) that minutes say would save about $100,000 a year {rso_min_20260414}.

Other decisions: in January 2026 the board approved a new Southeastern Career Center operating agreement and the addition of Madison Consolidated Schools as a member {rso_min_20260113}; in May 2026 it raised preschool and daycare fees to $30 a day for 2026-27 ($35 for children from outside the corporation) {rso_min_20260506}. In December 2025 the superintendent briefed the board on the state's new accountability model {rso_min_20251202}.
Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire or news coverage of this race.
